title: Corporate Forum
tagline: Full-auth internal discussion forum with admin moderation
description: A role-gated internal discussion platform built with Spring Security and Spring Data JDBC. Employees and managers self-register with access codes, then create threads and nested replies; admins can lock or delete any thread. Runs fully self-contained against an in-memory H2 database.
keyFeatures: Role-gated self-registration via access codes (employee vs. manager)
Threaded discussions with nested replies
Admin-only thread locking and deletion
Session-based authentication with Spring Security
Zero external setup: self-contained in-memory H2 database

star.situation: I'd used internal tools with role-based access plenty of times, but never built one, and I wanted to know what that took.
star.task: Build a role-gated discussion platform where employees and managers register with access codes and admins can moderate.
star.action: Built it with Spring Boot, Spring Security, and Spring Data JDBC, with self-registration via access codes, threaded discussions, and admin-only thread locking and deletion, running self-contained against an in-memory H2 database.
star.result: A fully working internal forum that needs zero external setup to run and demo.

title: NovaCore Forum
tagline: HTTPS-secured re-architecture of the corporate forum concept
description: A from-scratch reimplementation of the corporate forum concept, hardened with end-to-end TLS. Employees and admins authenticate over HTTPS with a self-signed certificate, and sessions are locked down with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict cookies.
keyFeatures: Full HTTPS with a self-signed PKCS12 keystore
Distinct employee and admin roles
Hardened session cookies (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict)
Admin-gated H2 console access
One-time-use registration access codes

star.situation: Corporate Forum worked, but it wasn't secure enough to trust with real employee credentials.
star.task: Rebuild the same concept from scratch, hardened for production-level security.
star.action: Added full HTTPS with a self-signed PKCS12 keystore, locked down session cookies with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict, gated the H2 console behind admin auth, and made registration codes one-time use.
star.result: A hardened version of the same forum, and the project where the security decisions finally made sense to me.

title: Thymeleaf Fragments Showcase
tagline: Modular server-rendered UI built from reusable Thymeleaf fragments
description: A focused demonstration of Thymeleaf's fragment composition model: a single product-listing page assembled at render time from independent head, body, and footer fragments, backed by a seeded in-memory catalog.
keyFeatures: Page composed from independent head/body/footer fragments
Demonstrates Thymeleaf's th:insert / th:replace composition model
Seeded product catalog on startup
No authentication layer: purely a templating-architecture example

star.situation: I wanted to properly understand Thymeleaf's fragment composition model instead of copying boilerplate without knowing why it worked.
star.task: Build something that used the pattern for real, rather than a project that only mentioned it in passing.
star.action: Built a single product-listing page assembled at render time from independent head, body, and footer fragments, backed by a seeded in-memory catalog.
star.result: A working demonstration of server-rendered fragment composition, and a pattern I can reuse directly on future Thymeleaf projects.

title: Role-Based Access Control Demo
tagline: Self-service registration with selectable USER / ADMIN authorities
description: A Spring Security demo where new users choose their own authority at registration time (USER, ADMIN, or both), and an ADMIN-gated products page enforces that choice. Served entirely over HTTPS with automatic HTTP-to-HTTPS redirection.
keyFeatures: Registration form with a selectable authority dropdown (USER / ADMIN / BOTH)
ADMIN-gated /secure/products route
HTTPS with automatic HTTP → HTTPS redirect
Authority-based route guarding with Spring Security

star.situation: Letting users choose their own role at signup is a common real-world pattern, and it's easy to get wrong.
star.task: Build a demo where the chosen role holds up on every protected route, well past the signup form that sets it.
star.action: Built a Spring Security app where new users pick USER, ADMIN, or both at registration, with an ADMIN-gated products page and automatic HTTP-to-HTTPS redirection.
star.result: A working reference for exactly how authority-based route guarding should behave.

title: In-Memory Security Config Demo
tagline: Minimal Spring Security setup with hardcoded in-memory users
description: The simplest possible Spring Security bootstrap: two hardcoded users defined directly in an InMemoryUserDetailsManager, no database at all, used to demonstrate role-based route protection and access-denied handling in isolation.
keyFeatures: Zero-database InMemoryUserDetailsManager configuration
Two roles demonstrated: ROLE_ADMIN and ROLE_USER
Access-denied handling for under-privileged users
Minimal reference implementation of Spring Security route guarding

star.situation: I wanted the simplest possible teaching example for Spring Security, without a database schema getting in the way.
star.task: Strip a real security setup down to its essential parts.
star.action: Built it with two hardcoded users in an InMemoryUserDetailsManager, demonstrating role-based route protection and access-denied handling.
star.result: The example I go back to whenever I need to explain Spring Security without a whiteboard's worth of schema.

title: Book Haven
tagline: Thymeleaf client performing full CRUD against a separate REST API
description: A two-service architecture: a Thymeleaf UI client that performs full CRUD on a book catalog purely by calling a separate, independently deployable REST API over HTTP via RestTemplate, with no shared database access between the two services.
keyFeatures: Two independently deployable Spring Boot services (UI client + REST API)
Full CRUD (create, read, update, delete) for a book catalog
UI talks to the API purely over HTTP via RestTemplate
Realistic client/server microservice split

star.situation: It's easy to build a fake microservice split where the UI secretly still shares a database with its 'API.'
star.task: Build two genuinely independent services that only talk to each other over HTTP.
star.action: Built a Thymeleaf UI client that performs full CRUD on a book catalog purely by calling a separate REST API via RestTemplate, with no shared database access between the two.
star.result: Two services that can be deployed and scaled independently, exactly like a real client/backend split.

title: Linux Network Services Lab
tagline: Core network services configured and validated in virtualized Linux environments
description: Configured and validated FTP, NFS, Samba, and Sendmail services across virtualized Linux environments, with attention to file permissions, service availability, and repeatable administration steps.
keyFeatures: FTP file transfer service configured with scoped user permissions
NFS shared storage mounted and validated across virtual hosts
Samba file sharing configured for cross-platform access
Sendmail mail transfer agent configured and tested end to end

star.situation: Most developers never touch the network layer their app runs on top of.
star.task: Configure that layer myself instead of treating it as someone else's problem.
star.action: Configured and validated FTP, NFS, Samba, and Sendmail across virtualized Linux environments, with attention to file permissions and repeatable administration steps.
star.result: I can now read a network-layer error and know what to check instead of guessing.
